messages:
maya_support: Heads-up: Customer Acme is hitting sustained 429s during peak traffic on their Dedicated pool (pool-id: ded-82). They report requests queueing ~6-12s then 429. They say retries still fail.
kevin_sre: Can you paste the request IDs / example logs? Also which model version and route are they on?
maya_support: route: /v1/generate (gpt-open-16k-v1), request_id samples: r-5d9f, r-5da0. Found this in our gateway logs:
```
[2026-02-28T15:02:11Z] r-5d9f 429 throttle: no available replica after 12000ms wait
[2026-02-28T15:02:12Z] r-5da0 200 served by replica r-9c3d latency 210ms
[2026-02-28T15:05:01Z] r-5f10 429 throttle: min_replicas reached
```
kevin_sre: "min_replicas reached" - that's interesting. Can you fetch the pool config and autoscaler events?
devin_platform: run: `redwoodctl get pool ded-82 -o yaml` and `redwoodctl describe autoscaler ded-82`
maya_support: did that, pasted outputs below (redacted):
```
pool:
  id: ded-82
  min_replicas: 2
  max_replicas: 20
  current_replicas: 2
  cooldown_seconds: 300
  burst_capacity: enabled
autoscaler events:
  - 2026-02-28T14:58:00 scale_request target=6 reason="cpu spike"
  - 2026-02-28T14:58:05 scale_blocked by_cooldown remaining=295s
  - 2026-02-28T15:03:05 scale_request target=6 reason="queue depth"
  - 2026-02-28T15:03:07 scale_blocked by_cooldown remaining=238s
```

anna_ops: Looks like cooldown is preventing further scale within 5m window. If current_replicas stayed at 2 that's expected behavior. How long did traffic stay high?
maya_support: traffic spiked ~14:57 to 15:10 (13 minutes), concurrent request rate ~3x baseline. They expect burst to 8-10 replicas.
priya_prod: Do we have any cloud quota/slow node provisioning messages? Sometimes GKE preemptible nodes take time and block scaling.
kevin_sre: Checked cloud provider events for the cluster: no quota limit reported. However, there are sporadic node provisioning delays in that region (eu-west-1c) around same timeframe. Node provisioning latency ~90-180s on some requests.
autoscale-bot: [AUTOSCALE] ded-82: scale to 6 requested at 2026-02-28T14:58:00, blocked by cooldown; next eligible: 2026-02-28T15:03:00
kevin_sre: So two issues stacking: conservative cooldown + slow node warmup/cold start for model containers. With min_replicas=2 and cooldown=300s any repeated surge within 5m won't increase quickly.
devin_platform: For dedicated we recommend smaller cooldown for latency-sensitive customers: 60-120s, and enabling warm standby containers (pre-warm) or burst_capacity config that allows ephemeral replicas without full node provisioning. Is burst_capacity actually kicking in?
maya_support: burst_capacity: enabled in config, but logs show provision attempts fallback to regular pool when burst exhausted. It looks like burst had only 1 warm slot and was consumed early.
anna_ops: Can you share the kernel/container startup logs? Cold starts for gpt-open-16k-v1 are ~8-12s once container scheduled, plus node bootstrap time.
maya_support: sample container log when scaling attempt happened:
```
[2026-02-28T14:58:07] pulled image
[2026-02-28T14:58:18] loaded model shard 1/4
[2026-02-28T14:58:32] healthcheck passed
```
So ~25s container readiness once node available. Node provisioning added another ~90s in some cases.
kevin_sre: That explains the 6-12s queue + later 429s once backlog exceeded queue timeout. Two fixes: 1) reduce cooldown to allow more aggressive scale-ups, 2) increase burst_capacity or scheduled pre-warms for known traffic windows, 3) bump min_replicas for this customer so baseline covers typical peaks.
priya_prod: Any cost constraints? Customer on committed Dedicated m3 plan, but they flagged cost concerns earlier and asked for tight min_replicas. We should propose an intermediate: scheduled scaling during their business hours + lower cooldown + add 2 warm standbys.
kevin_sre: Operational playbook also: add a short-term mitigation to manually trigger scale to 8 while we adjust autoscaler settings. I can run `redwoodctl scale pool ded-82 --replicas 8 --reason "support escal: pre-warm"` now.
devin_platform: I'll also check burst_capacity config and increase ephemeral slots to 4 for this pool. If node provisioning is the blocker, we can enable warm nodes in the same AZ or use faster node types.
maya_support: Repro steps I gave customer to validate after manual scale: they should hit the same route and look for 200s within <300ms and no 429s. Example curl: 
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" -d '{"prompt":"x","max_tokens":20}' https://ded-82.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -v
```
They'll run 50 concurrent clients to simulate peak.
anna_ops: Action items:
- kevin_sre: manually scale to 8 and monitor for 20m (assigned)
- devin_platform: increase burst_capacity ephemeral slots to 4, and lower cooldown to 90s (assigned)
- priya_prod: draft email to customer with recommended scheduled scaling plan and cost impact (assigned)
- maya_support: gather post-change logs and confirm customer test (assigned)

kevin_sre: Running manual scale now. command: `redwoodctl scale pool ded-82 --replicas 8 --note "pre-warm for Acme"`
autoscale-bot: [ACTION] manual scale executed by kevin_sre: pool ded-82 scaled from 2 -> 8 at 2026-02-28T15:07:30
kevin_sre: Monitoring. Initial telemetry shows queue depth dropping, 429s gone for past 3 minutes. Will keep watch and follow up.
maya_support: Customer confirmed reduced 429s, but noted slightly higher cost for the time window. They accepted scheduled scaling proposal if we can automate it.
priya_prod: I'll send the email with the proposed schedule and optional hourly costs.
kevin_sre: Postmortem note: consider lowering default cooldown for Dedicated pools used for low-latency production routes. Also, improve autoscaler heuristic to allow one emergency scale during cooldown if queue depth > X for >Y seconds. Creating follow-up ticket.
maya_support: Thanks team :thumbsup: I'll close the escalation when customer signs off."
